newsitem.title: LEBANON: Security tightened around Japan's Beirut embassy.
newsitem.headline: Security tightened around Japan's Beirut embassy.

text.p: Lebanon has tightened security around the Japanese embassy in east Beirut after Lebanese authorities arrested a number of Japanese Red Army suspects five days ago.

Witnesses on Thursday said two plainclothes state security men stood at the embassy's entrance and two more inside the compound while two others drove around the four-storey building in Baabda suburb in hills overlooking Beirut.
A Lebanese police patrol also circled the compound, 200 metres (yards) from Lebanon's presidential palace, five km (three miles) east of Beirut, they added.
Last Saturday, security forces arrested five Japanese Red Army suspects, three Japanese sympathisers and three Lebanese citizens in Beirut and the eastern Bekaa Valley.
Authoritative sources in Tokyo said on Wednesday that Japanese embassies around the world were asked to tighten security after the arrests.

The sources also said that Japan and Lebanon were discussing the deportation to Tokyo of the suspected guerrillas named in the media as Kazuo Tohira, 44, Hisashi Matsuda, 48, Mariko Yamamoto, 56, Masao Adachi, 57 and Kozo Okamoto, 49.

Lebanon justice ministry sources told Reuters that Japan's ambassador Yasujji Ishikagi expressed on Thursday his country's readiness to cooperate with the Lebanese judicial authorities in identifying the suspects.

The ambassador told Justice Minister Bahij Tabbara in Beirut that Tokyo would want to negotiate possible ways to extradite the suspects if it was proved that they were involved in terrorist acts, the sources added.
The Red Army, founded in 1971, is allied to hardline anti-Israeli Palestinian factions.
